item.title: How Much Tax Does the UK Actually Pay? 2026 Data Study
item.description:
Quick answer: A UK employee earning £35,000 pays approximately £9,620 in total deductions (income tax + NI + pension), an effective rate of 27.5%. Add VAT on spending (estimated £3,500/year) and council tax (~£2,000), and the total tax burden reaches roughly 38% of gross income. This data study breaks down every layer of UK taxation by salary level.

How Much Tax Does the UK Actually Pay? 2026 Data Study

Most people know their income tax and NI deductions from their payslip, but the full picture of UK taxation is much broader. This data study quantifies every major tax a typical UK employee pays across salary levels from £20,000 to £200,000.

item.title: UK Household Costs by Region 2026: Average Bills Compared
item.description:
Quick answer: The average UK household spends approximately £4,200–£4,800 per year on essential utilities (electricity, gas, water, council tax, and broadband). Costs vary significantly by region: London and the South East are most expensive, while Wales and the North East are cheapest. Council Tax accounts for the largest regional variation — a Band D property in Rutland pays roughly £2,300/year versus £1,200 in Westminster.
